frameworks.help: Install the base first, then pick one plugin stack. Almost every plugin depends on Metamod; the market uses CounterStrikeSharp. Do not mix CSS and SwiftlyS2 on the same server.
frameworks.secondaryHelp: Framework installs are long SSH jobs. Progress streams in the log on this page.
frameworks.baseHelp: Almost every plugin depends on the base framework. Metamod:Source is the Source 2 plugin loader. CounterStrikeSharp, CS2Fixes, and most market plugins sit on top of it. Install the base first, then a runtime or market plugins.
frameworks.purposeHelp: The base hooks plugins into the game process. Without Metamod most CS2 plugins cannot load. CounterStrikeSharp runs market C# plugins. CS2Fixes adds gameplay fixes. SwiftlyS2 is a separate runtime.
frameworks.recommendHelp: Default path: Metamod → CounterStrikeSharp. That is what the plugin market and most community plugins expect. Add CS2Fixes only if you need those fixes. Choose SwiftlyS2 only when you specifically need Swiftly plugins.
frameworks.conflictHelp: Keep one plugin stack per server. CounterStrikeSharp / CS2Fixes and SwiftlyS2 hook the same game surface. Mixing them leaves plugins unloaded or the server unstable.
frameworks.stackHelp: Install the recommended stack as 1, 2, then 3. If Metamod is missing when you install CounterStrikeSharp, the panel adds the base automatically.
frameworks.streamHelp: Install or update a base / framework and watch progress here.
frameworks.streamEmpty: Progress appears here after you start an install or update above.
frameworks.recommendedPath: 1. Metamod:Source (base, required) → 2. CounterStrikeSharp (most market plugins) → 3. CS2Fixes if you need it. Installing CSS also installs Metamod when it is missing.
frameworks.alternatePath: SwiftlyS2 is a standalone C#/Lua runtime and can run without Metamod. It conflicts with CounterStrikeSharp and CS2Fixes — pick one stack per server.
frameworks.backupHelp: Snapshot the plugin directory so you can roll back a bad framework or plugin install.
frameworks.conflictLive: This host already has {other} on record. Installing {name} will conflict — keep one plugin stack per server.

metamod.name: Metamod:Source

metamod.purpose: Purpose: inject plugins into CS2. Install first. No conflicts.

counterstrikesharp.summary: C# runtime for market plugins. Depends on Metamod.
counterstrikesharp.purpose: Purpose: run market C# plugins. Default recommended stack. Conflicts with SwiftlyS2.

cs2fixes.purpose: Purpose: patch issues Valve has not fixed. Fine next to CounterStrikeSharp. Conflicts with SwiftlyS2.

swiftly.summary: Standalone C#/Lua runtime. Not the market default.
swiftly.purpose: Purpose: only when you need Swiftly plugins. Conflicts with CounterStrikeSharp and CS2Fixes — do not mix.

tutorial.title: How to deploy a CS2 game server with this panel
tutorial.subtitle: Lightweight hosts, Tencent Cloud, Aliyun, Google Cloud, and Amazon Cloud follow the same steps. This walkthrough uses Aliyun. Panel screenshots show the current Next console.
tutorial.chinaSteamWarning: Mainland China hosts can download from Steam very slowly. You can deploy your own proxy gateway. That is not a panel bug; the steps follow Valve documentation.
tutorial.step1Body: When buying the cloud host, pick Ubuntu 24.04 64-bit and give the system disk at least 100 GiB. Other providers use the same spec.
tutorial.step2Body: Choose a custom password, select root as the login name, and set the password. The panel uses these credentials for host initialization.
tutorial.step3Body: Add an inbound security-group rule: UDP (at least 27015, or all UDP) from 0.0.0.0/0. Keep SSH 22 open as well.
tutorial.step4Body: Open Servers → Initialize host, enter the root SSH details, and start automatic setup. The panel creates the cs2server user, installs packages, and fixes directory permissions.
tutorial.step5Title: Enter SSH details and start automatic setup
tutorial.step5Body: Fill in the root SSH details, complete the captcha, and start automatic setup. When it finishes, copy the cs2server username, password, and game directory immediately. Saved accounts stay in Redis for about 24 hours.
tutorial.step6Title: Add the server to the panel
tutorial.step6Body: On Add server, pick the host you just initialized, confirm the IP, SSH user (cs2server), and game directory, then submit.
tutorial.step8Body: On the servers list, click Manage server to enter that host's workspace. The left navigation stays available so you can return to Overview anytime.
tutorial.step9Body: In the operations center, click Deploy. The job enters the delivery queue — do not wait on the form. Jobs on the same host run one at a time.
tutorial.step10Body: The activity tray in the top-right shows the submitted command, status, and live log. After deploy finishes you can start the server, install plugins, or open the console.

serverHelp.execstackIssue: glibc 2.41 is stricter about dynamic libraries that request an executable stack, so older .so files can be rejected by dlopen.
serverHelp.execstackWhy: This is separate from missing libssl1.1: the executable-stack restriction can make older libraries fail dlopen, while libssl1.1 supplies the legacy OpenSSL runtime. Only plugins with these legacy requirements are affected.

serverHelp.execstackNote: The command edits the selected plugin in place; run it again after plugin updates. Plugins that truly require an executable stack should be upgraded to an upstream fixed build.
